title: Committee of Supply – Head V (Ministry of Trade and Industry)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head V (Ministry of Trade and Industry)

sections.label: Growing economy and social compact
sections.summary: A motion to reduce Head V of the Estimates by $100, stating a growing economy is needed for jobs and resources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head V of the Estimates be reduced by $100." Sir, having a growing and vibrant economy is very much a part of our efforts to build a strong social compact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: We need a growing economy to create good, fulfilling jobs for Singaporeans and to generate the resources to tackle our social and longer-term challenges.

sections.label: Singapore FDI and BEPS Pillar Two
sections.summary: Singapore is the world's fourth largest recipient of FDIs, and BEPS Pillar Two will reset investment competition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Despite being a small economy, Singapore is the fourth largest recipients of foreign direct investments (FDIs) in the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: However, the implementation of Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) Pillar Two will reset the playing field in the competition for investments and would have implications in our efforts to attract high-quality and high-value investments.

sections.label: Financial hub and development fund
sections.summary: Singapore's financial hub position is hard to replicate, and $2 billion was injected into the Financial Sector Development Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The one services sector that plays to our strengths and not easily replicable by others is our premiere position as a financial hub and as the international financial centre of the East.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: I am glad we are not resting on our laurels and have announced another $2-billion injection into the Financial Sector Development Fund to further up our game in this year's Budget.

sections.label: LNG terminal, energy fund, competitiveness questions
sections.summary: Moves include a second LNG terminal and a $5-billion Future Energy Fund, with questions on competitiveness, enterprises, manufacturing and partnerships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Some of the major moves include building a second liquefied natural gas (LNG) terminal as well as the setting up of the Future Energy Fund with an initial $5-billion injection to further develop the critical infrastructure and to transit to clean energy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: We are investing big time to grow our own timber, such as the SkillsFuture Level-Up, Career Health and others; but we have also got to be open to have external workforce that complements and strengthens our overall proposition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: First, given these unsettling times, how is the Government ensuring that Singapore will remain globally competitive and relevant?

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Second, how does MTI plan to continue supporting our enterprises, to capture future growth opportunities in the region and in growth sectors such as AI and the green economy?

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Third, can the Government share more about its plans to enhance the competitiveness of the manufacturing sector?

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Fourth, to strengthen our connectivity and international linkages, can the Minister share more details on our international collaboration efforts and how Singapore companies can benefit from these partnerships?

sections.label: SMEs facing growth challenges
sections.summary: SMEs, the majority of the business landscape, face challenges threatening their growth and sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Chairman, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) forming the majority of our business landscape are currently navigating a myriad of challenges that threaten their growth and sustainability.

sections.label: SME criterion for MNE grants
sections.summary: Welcoming the expanded Partnerships for Capability Transformation scheme, proposing SME involvement as a criterion for MNEs accessing Government grants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong rightly pointed out that, "We cannot force MNEs to choose only local suppliers, but we can and we will help Singapore enterprises to meet the high standards and to form win-win partnerships with MNEs." I welcome the expansion of the Partnerships for Capability Transformation scheme to encompass broader areas of collaboration.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, to further enhance this initiative, I propose that the Government consider an additional step – and this is an important step – by integrating the involvement of Singapore-based SMEs as a positive criterion for multinational enterprises (MNEs) and larger corporations when they access Government grants.

sections.label: Enterprise Singapore loan risk sharing
sections.summary: Enterprise Singapore shares loan default risk with participating financial institutions, with Government risk sharing reaching up to 70%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: A key feature is its risk sharing component, where Enterprise Singapore shares the loan default risk with participating financial institutions in the event of enterprise insolvency.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Government's risk sharing can reach up to 70%, therefore providing a significant safety net for banks.

sections.label: SME loan terms support
sections.summary: The question asks how the Government can help SMEs get more favourable interest rates, security requirements and payment terms on EFS loans versus standard bank loans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: How can the Government support SMEs to secure more favourable interest rates, more flexible security requirements and more favourable payment terms for those that are on EFS loans versus those that are on standard bank loans?

sections.label: GDP growth plans amid ageing
sections.summary: The question cites studies on super ageing Japan's GDP drop and asks the Ministry for its 10-year plans to grow GDP despite constraints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Studies have shown that super ageing Japan's GDP was expected to drop by about 5% relative to the baseline scenario of a stationary population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry share what are its overarching plans over the next 10 years to grow our GDP despite our constraints?

sections.label: A*STAR T-UP take-up
sections.summary: The question asks for an update on take-up of the A*STAR T-UP programme and how to improve take-up by SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry provide an update on the take-up of the Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR) T-UP programme and how can we continue to improve take-up by SMEs?

sections.label: Refundable Investment Tax Credit
sections.summary: The passage states that the Refundable Investment Tax Credit is very welcome.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Refundable Investment Tax Credit is therefore very welcome.

sections.label: Scheme investment attractiveness question
sections.summary: The question asks how the scheme will keep Singapore attractive as an investment destination given measures other jurisdictions are putting in place.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: One, how will the scheme keep Singapore attractive as an investment destination when taking into account the measures that other jurisdictions are putting into place?

sections.label: Green economy and sustainability support
sections.summary: Southeast Asia's Internet economy is forecasted to reach US$1 trillion by 2030 and over five to six million new jobs are expected from the green economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Southeast Asia's Internet economy is forecasted to reach US$1 trillion by 2030 and over five to six million new jobs are expected to be created through the green economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In Singapore itself, we expect to create more than 50,000 green jobs by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2023, MTI announced enhanced support under the Enterprise Development Grant for sustainability projects to support more firms in capturing new growth opportunities in sustainability as we transition to a green economy.

sections.label: Free Trade Agreements and internationalisation schemes
sections.summary: Singapore has 27 implemented FTAs and is a signatory to regional agreements, with MTI, Enterprise Singapore and SBF offering internationalisation schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Today, we have forged an extensive network of 27 implemented Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) along with being a signatory to many regional agreements in the Asia Pacific like the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership and the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On its part, MTI, Enterprise Singapore and the Singapore Business Federation (SBF) also offer several schemes and programmes, such as the Global Innovation Alliance, to support companies' internationalisation efforts.

sections.label: Risk of economic coercion
sections.summary: With these, come greater risk of Singapore facing economic coercion.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: With these, come greater risk of Singapore facing economic coercion.

sections.label: Preparing for economic pressure
sections.summary: The passage asks what concrete efforts are being taken to prepare for and mitigate economic pressure, alone and with partners.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: What are the concrete efforts being taken to prepare for and mitigate economic pressure that may come our way, both on our own and in conjunction with partners?

sections.label: Migrant worker recruitment fees
sections.summary: Migrant workers pay recruitment fees up to $12,000, and the Workers' Party calls for a Government jobs portal and asks if MOM and MTI engage source countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Migrant workers continue to pay high recruitment fees of up to $12,000 to have the opportunity to work in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party reiterates our call for the creation of a Government jobs' portal that advertises all open positions for migrant workers to cut fees workers pay to agents in Singapore and overseas.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is also said that we have no legal jurisdiction to influence the recruitment fees migrant workers pay in their home countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But are MOM and MTI engaging with source countries on the recruitment fee issue, given the impact that it will have on MNCs' supply chains in Singapore?

sections.label: MTI adapting regionalisation programmes
sections.summary: The passage asks how MTI is adapting programmes such as Scale-up to align with the evolving external environment and keep regionalisation support effective.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In light of these changes, how is MTI adapting its programmes – such as Scale-up – to align with this evolving external environment, ensuring that support for regionalisation remains effective?

sections.label: Tourism recovery and local content
sections.summary: MTI is asked for strategies to restore tourism to pre-pandemic levels and initiatives to boost local content and IPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Despite efforts, tourism arrival figures and projections have yet to rebound to pre-pandemic levels of 19 million per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: While the sector witnessed a robust resurgence in the past two years – largely attributable to schemes like the Jobs Support Scheme (JSS) that retains capabilities and capacities – other global tourism hubs have regained momentum and competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In light of these circumstances, what are MTI's specific strategies to restore our tourism sector to pre-pandemic levels?

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Furthermore, within these strategies, what specific initiatives are in place to enhance local content; empowering local enterprises to cultivate robust Intellectual Properties (IPs) instead of solely relying on imported IPs?

sections.label: SME digitalisation and AI
sections.summary: MTI is asked to share plans to help SMEs accelerate digitalisation so more local businesses can use AI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In this regard, can MTI share its plans to help SMEs further accelerate their digitalisation so that more local businesses can harness AI to transform and increase productivity?

sections.label: SME sustainability grants and ESG
sections.summary: MTI is asked to assess existing grants like the Enterprise Sustainability Programme and how to enhance them for SMEs' ESG goals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Yet, while advancing in the green journey is essential and more Government funding is available, a DBS study in 2023 found that only 37% of SMEs had a clear roadmap on how to achieve their sustainability goals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: On this note, what is MTI's assessment of the progress and effectiveness of existing grants and initiatives, such as the Enterprise Sustainability Programme and how may they be enhanced to help our SMEs be more ESG-savvy?

sections.label: SME Centres advisory and KPIs
sections.summary: MTI is asked whether there are plans to boost SME Centres' advisory capabilities and align KPIs with outcomes like productivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One, whether there are plans to boost the effectiveness of SME Centres by enhancing its advisory capabilities and sharpening its own key performance indicators (KPIs) from Level 1 or baseline targets, such as number of SME visits, to be more aligned with the outcomes, such as SME productivity and customer growth of the portfolio of SMEs they cover?

sections.label: AI initiatives and sandboxes
sections.summary: MTI has launched initiatives including AI Innovation sandboxes, hands-on workshops, and the AI Trailblazers initiative for GenAI use cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: MTI has launched a number of good initiatives, such as AI Innovation sandboxes and hands-on workshops aimed at identifying AI and GenAI use cases; and the AI Trailblazers initiative, which helps organisations to identify GenAI use cases and build solution prototypes.

sections.label: Tetra Pak closure affects workers
sections.summary: The closure of Tetra Pak will affect 300 workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The closure of Tetra Pak will affect 300 workers.

sections.label: SME sustainability and confidence surveys
sections.summary: A DBS survey found 63% of Asian SMEs cited transitioning to a sustainable business model as their top challenge, and a Singapore Business Review survey reported 58% of small and microbusinesses less confident about 2024 prospects.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: Yet, a DBS survey found that 63% of SMEs in Asia identified as their top challenge transitioning to a sustainable business model.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: In a survey reported in the Singapore Business Review last month, 58% of small and microbusinesses polled are less confident about prospects in 2024.

sections.label: Cash versus reimbursement grants
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Government could provide some grants on a cash rather than reimbursement basis to help firms that would not normally consider environmental matters in cashflow planning.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: Could the Government provide some of these grants on a cash rather than a reimbursement basis, to help firms who would not normally look at environmental matters in their cashflow planning?

sections.label: Our Heartlands 2025 launch
sections.summary: In 2022, MTI and Enterprise Singapore launched the Our Heartlands 2025 initiative to revitalise local neighborhoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
sentences.text: In 2022, MTI and Enterprise Singapore launched "Our Heartlands 2025" initiative to revitalise local neighborhoods.

sections.label: Progress of heartland initiatives
sections.summary: The speaker applauds Government initiatives for heartland shops and asks the Minister to share the progress of Our Heartlands 2025 and Heartlands Go Digital, noting MTI and Enterprise Singapore launched Our Heartlands 2025 in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: I applaud the Government in launching various initiatives to energise and support our heartland shops.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask the Minister to share the progress of "Our Heartlands 2025" and "Heartlands Go Digital".

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, coming out of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2022, MTI and Enterprise Singapore launched the "Our Heartlands 2025" initiative to boost the growth and efficiency of our heartland shops which had demonstrated “incredible resilience and mettle to transform and thrive” during the pandemic.

sections.label: Manufacturing share and company moves
sections.summary: Manufacturing accounts for about one-fifth of annual GDP and around 11% to 14% of jobs in the last 10 years, with Dyson, Hyundai and GlobalFoundries opening or planning advanced manufacturing plants in Singapore, while IBM, Coca Cola and AU Optronics closed facilities here in the past decade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: After all, manufacturing accounts for approximately one-fifth of our annual GDP and around 11% to 14% of jobs in the last 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Dyson, Hyundai and GlobalFoundries are just some of the big names that have recently opened or announced plans to open advanced manufacturing plants in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: However, in the past decade, companies, such as IBM, Coca Cola and display maker AU Optronics, have closed their multi-million-dollar manufacturing facilities here as well.

sections.label: Tourism recovery and funding
sections.summary: The pandemic affected tourism flows and Singapore, but with Singapore Tourism Board support tourism receipts bounced back to an estimated $14 billion in 2023, and in 2022 MTI announced half a billion dollars earmarked for tourism recovery.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
sentences.text: The pandemic had impacted tourism flows across the world and also affected Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
sentences.text: However, with support from the Singapore Tourism Board, tourism receipts have bounced back to an estimated $14 billion in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
sentences.text: In 2022, MTI announced that the Government had earmarked half a billion dollars to support tourism recovery.

sections.label: Creative sectors value added
sections.summary: MCCY said nominal value added from three sectors rose from $7.9 billion in 2017 to $11.7 billion in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY), in response to a Parliamentary Question filed by me earlier this year, the nominal value added from these three sectors increased by close to 50% over the past five years and the increase was from $7.9 billion in 2017 to $11.7 billion in 2022.

sections.label: MTI creative economy spending
sections.summary: The question asks MTI how much expenditure will go to Singapore's creative economy and profiling it as a creative destination.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could MTI clarify how much of its own development or other expenditure will be allocated to the growth and development of Singapore's creative economy in the coming financial year?

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can we expect to see more expenditure in the profiling of Singapore as a premier destination for creative and cultural consumption?

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We saw this very recently with the Taylor Swift Eras Tour concert and the Government's outreach to Swift's team.

sections.label: RIE2025 additional $3 billion
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong announced an additional $3 billion for the Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2025 Plan in Budget 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, to enhance Singapore's R&D efforts, Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong announced additional investments of $3 billion to the Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2025 Plan (RIE2025) in Budget 2024.

sections.label: Local enterprise R&D growth
sections.summary: Under the RIE, local enterprises' R&D business expenditure rose from $1.1 billion in 2010 to $1.6 billion in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Under the RIE, local enterprises' business expenditure on R&D increased from $1.1 billion in 2010 to $1.6 billion in 2020, while the number of local enterprises involved in research and development grew from approximately 450 to almost 600 now.

sections.label: Long Island reclamation announcement
sections.summary: Three months ago it was announced a new 'Long Island' will be reclaimed off Singapore's eastern coast, expected to be double Marina Bay's size.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Three months ago, it was announced that we will reclaim and create a new "Long Island" off Singapore's eastern coast, expected to be double the size of Marina Bay.

sections.label: Power sector emissions share
sections.summary: Singapore's power sector makes up 40% of the country's emissions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Singapore's power sector makes up 40% of our emissions.

sections.label: Future Energy Fund announcement
sections.summary: In Budget 2024, Deputy Prime Minister Wong announced the new Future Energy Fund with a $5 billion injection to help Singapore transition to cleaner energy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: In Budget 2024, Deputy Prime Minister Wong announced the new Future Energy Fund with an injection of $5 billion to help the nation transition towards cleaner energy sources.

sections.label: Foreign fusion energy investments
sections.summary: The UK, US, China and Japan have announced funding, targets or facilities for fusion energy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: The United Kingdom (UK) has announced an additional $1.1 billion equivalent, in additional funding for its fusion programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: President Biden has set a "Decadal Vision" for the US to produce commercial fusion energy by 2032.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: China has invested more than $1 billion dollars in fusion research and Japan has recently launched the world's biggest experimental fusion reactor.

sections.label: Businesses and clean energy imports
sections.summary: The business community welcomes the $5 billion Future Energy Fund, while some businesses pioneer clean energy import projects like a subsea cable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee
sentences.text: Chairman, the business community welcomes the Government's commitment through the $5 billion Future Energy Fund aimed at bolstering clean energy initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee
sentences.text: Yet several businesses are already pioneering projects to import clean energy into Singapore, such as building a high-voltage subsea cable between Singapore and our neighbour.

sections.label: Energy Efficiency Grant questions
sections.summary: The speaker asks about projected energy savings from EEG-supported equipment purchases and MTI's target for savings under the expanded EEG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: Earlier this month, I asked a Parliamentary Question on the status of the EEG and the Minister shared that Enterprise Singapore has approved nearly 5,000 applications for the EEG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: What is the total projected energy savings from equipment purchases supported by the grant thus far?

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: Also, what is MTI's target for the total energy savings with the expanded EEG?

sections.label: Prepayment losses and used cars
sections.summary: CASE reported a 24% rise in prepayment losses in 2022, and consignment used car purchases do not fall under the lemon law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Consumers Association of Singapore (CASE) reported a 24% year-on-year increase in prepayment losses in 2022, with consumers reporting more than $645,000 in losses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Moreover, even though many used cars are sold by dealers on a consignment basis, unbeknownst to many consumers, such purchases do not fall under the "lemon law" – ironic, given the prevalence of lemons in the used car industry.

sections.label: Shrinkflation and unit pricing
sections.summary: The speaker asks MTI to work with CASE on shrinkflation and unit pricing, noting CASE's Price Kaki unit pricing and a 47% rise in e-commerce complaints in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: To address the issue of shrinkflation, where retailers seemingly maintain the price of a product but secretly reduces the portion size, can MTI work with CASE to examine the prevalence of this practice in Singapore and encourage local retailers to deploy unit pricing in-store?

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Since 1 January 2023, CASE has rolled out unit pricing on more than 6,000 items listed on the Price Kaki app.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to CASE's annual complaint statistics, the number of complaints relating to e-commerce transactions surged by 47% in 2023.

sections.label: Consumer Protection Act review
sections.summary: The Consumer Protection (Fair Trading) Act was last reviewed in 2016, before e-commerce boomed, and MTI is urged to review it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The Consumer Protection (Fair Trading) Act was last reviewed in 2016, a time when e-commerce had yet to boom in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I urge MTI to review the Act to account for the evolution in consumers' purchase habits.

sections.label: 2023 growth and 2024 outlook
sections.summary: The economy grew 1.1% in 2023, and for 2024 GDP growth is expected between 1% and 3% with moderating inflation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Amidst these challenges, our economy grew 1.1% in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: For 2024, we expect our GDP to grow by between 1% and 3% and inflation to moderate.

sections.label: Enterprise Support Package funding
sections.summary: $1.3 billion is being set aside for the Enterprise Support Package to address near-term challenges for enterprises.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Mr Shawn Huang asked about support for enterprises.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We are setting aside $1.3 billion for the Enterprise Support Package to address these near-term challenges.

sections.label: Corporate income tax rebate
sections.summary: Companies due for corporate income tax in Year of Assessment 2024 get a 50% rebate capped at $40,000, with a $2,000 minimum payout for those employing a local employee in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Companies due for corporate income tax in Year of Assessment 2024 will receive a 50% rebate, subject to a cap of $40,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: To ensure that smaller companies, even those that pay little or no income tax, can also benefit from the rebate, companies that employed at least one local employee in 2023 will receive a minimum cash payout of $2,000.

sections.label: GUTC four strategies
sections.summary: GUTC means four strategies: Grow our economy, Unlock our resource potential, Transform our businesses, and Connect to strengthen our status as a global business hub.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: By GUTC, we mean four strategies: Grow our economy; Unlock our resource potential; Transform our businesses; and Connect to strengthen our status as a global business hub and, therefore, GUTC.

sections.label: FDI growth
sections.summary: FDI grew by over 50%, from $1.9 trillion five years ago to approximately $2.9 trillion as at end of 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: FDI has grown by over 50%, from $1.9 trillion five years ago, to reach approximately $2.9 trillion as at end of 2023.

sections.label: ASEAN trade in goods growth
sections.summary: ASEAN trade in goods grew about 30% from US$645 billion in 2018 to US$857 billion in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Within ASEAN, trade in goods grew by about 30% from US$645 billion in 2018 to US$857 billion in 2022.

sections.label: New Refundable Investment Credit
sections.summary: A new Refundable Investment Credit will be introduced to enhance the investment promotion toolkit, as announced by Deputy Prime Minister Wong.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: First, as announced by Deputy Prime Minister Wong, we will enhance our investment promotion toolkit by introducing a new Refundable Investment Credit (RIC).

sections.label: AI growth and adoption plans
sections.summary: AI market size is projected to grow from US$150 billion in 2023 to US$1.35 trillion in 2030, and 100 companies will be partnered to build AI capabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The unprecedented growth of AI will accelerate in the coming years, with its market size projected to rocket from US$150 billion in 2023 to US$1.35 trillion in 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We will take both a company and sectoral approach to drive AI adoption.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We will partner 100 companies to build internal AI capabilities, develop and adopt AI solutions.

sections.label: Marine shipyard Dependency Ratio Ceiling
sections.summary: The marine shipyard sector's concessionary Dependency Ratio Ceiling will be adjusted from 3.5:1 to 3:1 in 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: To catalyse this shift, we will adjust the marine shipyard sector's concessionary Dependency Ratio Ceiling (DRC), from a ratio of 3.5:1 to 3:1 in 2026.

sections.label: M&OE Support Package and offshore wind
sections.summary: The M&OE Support Package will provide around $100 million over five years, and offshore wind is being explored as a growth opportunity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We aim to facilitate 100 new PACT partnerships over the next five years.

sections.label: EMA electricity market guardrails

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: These include: one, introducing a centralised process to facilitate and guide private investments in new generation capacities; two, placing more stringent regulatory requirements on electricity retailers to better protect consumers; and three, implementing a Temporary Price Cap mechanism to mitigate extreme price volatilities in the wholesale electricity market.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This year, we will also centralise the procurement of natural gas to ensure longer-term fuel adequacy for our power plants.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Last year, EMA granted Conditional Approvals to import up to 4.2 GW of low-carbon electricity from Cambodia, Indonesia and Vietnam.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)

sentences.text: We will continue to grow our ecosystem with our industry partners to better support the trade of goods and services that contribute to climate action – and make Singapore the heart of sustainable trade flows.

sections.label: MTI growing the economy

sections.label: Natural gas power generation
sections.summary: About 95% of Singapore's power generation needs come from natural gas.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Today, Mr Chairman, about 95% of our power generation needs come from natural gas.

sections.label: Second LNG terminal and energy security
sections.summary: Imports of 4.2 GW would be about 30% of energy needs by 2035, and a second LNG terminal would allow full non-dependence on piped natural gas.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: If Members look at the time horizon, our imports – at 4.2 GW for the conditional approvals that we have given – would constitute about 30% of our overall energy needs, and that is by 2035.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, as we ramp up from now to 2035, we will need to factor in the building of a second LNG terminal, in part, due to our own need for energy security, because that second LNG terminal would then allow us, supplemented by the existing LNG terminal that we have today, to be completely non-dependent on piped natural gas, and all of the LNG that comes in through ships and so on, can then fulfil 100% of our gas energy needs.

sections.label: Energy security and asset stranding
sections.summary: Energy security, reliability and resilience are of utmost importance, and the second LNG terminal would not run a significant risk of asset stranding.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, for us, energy security, reliability and our resilience are of utmost importance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: And when we did the projection with the increase in terms of our consumption, the second LNG terminal would not run a significant risk of asset stranding, even if we were to completely transition into all renewable energy, which is unlikely to be the case.

sentences.text: Even after they have come into Singapore and they have invested here, we continue to encourage them through different schemes, like PACT, as I mentioned; R&D schemes, to encourage them to have collaboration with local industries.

sections.label: Enhanced support for more sectors
sections.summary: From 1 April, local food services, retail and manufacturing companies will be able to enjoy enhanced support of 70%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: We want to continue to avail this to other sectors as well.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: That is why from 1 April, local food services, retail and manufacturing companies will be able to enjoy this enhanced support of 70%.
